(1) the physical environment of DSCUs has a positive impact on resident behavior, and (2) social environment factors such as staff-resident interactions and the quality of the social milieu are critical for the well-being of residents with dementia.

(1) the physical environment is important to the quality of life of residents with dementia, and (2) the social environment, particularly the quality of staff-resident interactions, is a critical factor in determining whether a DSCU is a successful intervention.

(1) physical and social environments can be designed to promote well-being and quality of life for individuals with dementia; (2) the environments of DSCUs differ significantly from those of traditional nursing homes, with the former providing greater opportunities for residents to engage in preferred activities and to interact with staff and other residents, as well as more privacy and control over their daily lives; and (3) the environments of nursing homes can be improved to better meet the needs of individuals with dementia.
